task_title: Phase P05 — Durable question mapping and assessment integrity

workstreams.title: Inventory and preservation baseline
steps: Document the current data paths from question-bank CRUD and assessment authoring through learner session creation, answer submission, grading, mastery updates, and result rendering.

On a read-only approved source or disposable clone, inventory counts and relationships for content_questions, question_skills, content_assessments, assessment_attempts, assessment_responses, content_revisions, and VNHSGE/source batches; record orphan, duplicate, null-mapping, and conflicting-ID cases without modifying records.
Define preservation invariants for every existing question ID, code, assessment link, attempt ID, response, score, revision, source batch, copyright field, and VNHSGE provenance field.
Confirm that QuestionSkill is the existing relational foundation and reuse it instead of retaining MetadataJson substring matching as the authoritative skill mapping.
Record compatibility requirements for legacy ContentQuestion.AssessmentId, local attempt cache, existing API consumers, and completed historical attempts before schema work begins.

workstreams.title: Durable keys, fingerprints, and duplicate prevention
steps: Add an immutable durable QuestionKey, a versioned normalization algorithm identifier, a SHA-256 content fingerprint, and SQL Server RowVersion to ContentQuestion; compute them server-side only.

Define QuestionKey from verified source identity when available, such as source type plus external/source item key; assign deterministic legacy keys based on existing immutable IDs where no trustworthy external key exists. Never rewrite existing primary keys or VNHSGE identifiers.

Canonicalize type, prompt, ordered options, verified answer representation, grade, and curriculum context before hashing. Keep the algorithm deterministic and versioned, and never log answer-bearing fingerprint input.
Backfill new columns additively. Preserve pre-existing duplicate rows as distinct historical records, emit a collision report, and never merge, delete, or repoint their attempts automatically.

Add filtered uniqueness for active durable keys and indexed fingerprint lookup. Enforce duplicate rejection transactionally on create, update, import, and assessment authoring, returning a conflict with safe canonical-record metadata.
Replace prompt-lowercase and optional-code duplicate checks with the durable key/fingerprint service while retaining explicit compatibility handling for legacy imports and concurrent insert races.

workstreams.title: Canonical lesson, skill, curriculum, and assessment mappings
steps: Make QuestionSkill the authoritative many-to-many question-to-skill mapping with validated foreign keys and unique QuestionId/SkillId pairs; expose ordered skill IDs/codes through management DTOs.

Validate that every mapped skill belongs to the same curriculum as the selected lesson and that lesson, chapter, subject, grade, and curriculum resolve through canonical foreign keys. Derive denormalized compatibility fields server-side instead of trusting request IDs.
Remove MetadataJson, Topic, Code substring searches from skill filtering and mastery evidence. Retain MetadataJson unchanged for backward compatibility but treat it as non-authoritative.

Remove import heuristics that infer hardcoded sub_math12 or other subject IDs from prompt/code text. Unresolved mappings must remain explicit validation errors or quarantined draft records, never silently fabricated relationships.

Introduce an assessment-question join entity containing AssessmentId, QuestionId, order, pinned question version/fingerprint, and RowVersion so a question can be reused without changing its identity. Backfill every legacy non-null ContentQuestion.AssessmentId association without dropping the legacy column in P05.

Require published assessments to contain only approved/published, provenance-complete questions with valid lesson/skill/curriculum mappings. Prevent unlinking or destructive mutation when historical attempts reference the mapping.

workstreams.title: Zero-loss migration and historical grading snapshots
steps: Create an additive P05 migration for question identity, assessment-question mappings, attempt question snapshots, concurrency tokens, indexes, and constraints; do not drop or rename existing question, attempt, response, or score columns.

At attempt creation, persist an ordered internal snapshot of the selected question version, fingerprint, answer key, grading rule, and assessment pass policy. Learner projections must never include protected snapshot fields before finalization.

Backfill historical assessment mappings and attempt snapshots from the best available current question/revision data, label the provenance as legacy backfill, and preserve stored scores and IsCorrect values rather than regrading history.

Use staged nullable columns and deterministic backfill before enforcing non-null constraints. If any row cannot be mapped safely, retain it, report it, and block constraint tightening instead of inventing a lesson, skill, curriculum, or answer.

Rehearse Up/Down/Up only against uniquely owned disposable StudyAIDb_Clean_{GUID} databases containing representative legacy duplicates, completed attempts, VNHSGE questions, revisions, and orphan cases; compare row counts, IDs, relationships, score values, and source metadata before and after.
Review generated SQL for table rebuilds, cascades, truncation, lossy conversions, or destructive Down operations and prepare a separately approved production migration and rollback runbook.

workstreams.title: Server-authoritative assessment lifecycle and immutability
steps: Replace client-authoritative attempt writes with explicit start, save-answer, resume, and finalize commands. Ignore or reject client-supplied UserId, score, IsCorrect, success status, completed timestamp, assessment identity, lesson identity, and subject identity.
Resolve the authenticated user from claims, verify assessment publication and availability, create the ordered snapshot server-side, and enforce ownership on every attempt and response operation.

Add an explicit attempt state machine and RowVersion. Allow edits only while in progress; make finalize transactional and idempotent; reject stale writes and every post-finalization answer, metadata, score, or identity mutation with HTTP 409.

Grade exclusively against the internal pinned snapshot, calculate score/pass state on the server, persist responses and aggregate results atomically, and update mastery only after successful finalization.
Add uniqueness and concurrency protection for attempt number/idempotency keys so retries cannot create duplicate attempts or double-apply mastery evidence.
Keep historical finalized attempts readable but immutable. Administrative correction, if required later, must be a separate audited compensating workflow rather than editing the original result.

workstreams.title: Answer-key isolation, RBAC, provenance, and audit
steps: Split staff authoring DTOs from learner question DTOs. Pre-finalization learner responses may contain prompt, safe media, choices, type, and display metadata only—never CorrectAnswer, explanation containing the answer, grading rules, internal fingerprint material, or protected snapshot data.

Allow answer/explanation review only after the owned attempt is finalized, or after an explicitly submitted practice question where immediate feedback is permitted by server-recorded mode. Prevent direct question-check endpoints from revealing answers for active assessments.
Authorize content draft CRUD to ContentAuthor scope, enforce independent reviewer/admin permissions for approve/publish/unpublish, and prohibit self-review where the existing four-eyes rule applies.

Add RowVersion to question and assessment mutations and return HTTP 409 for stale edits. Published content must be versioned or unpublished before answer-bearing fields, mappings, or pass policy change.

Require source type, source identity, license/copyright state, review actor, and mapping completeness before publication. VNHSGE records retain their original source batch, license proof, source URL, code, and content history.

Write StaffAuditLog entries in the same successful transaction for duplicate decisions, mapping changes, assessment composition changes, workflow transitions, archival, and exceptional administrative actions; exclude student answers, answer keys, credentials, and private data.
Return consistent 400, 401, 403, 404, and 409 semantics and never report success when grading, persistence, mastery update, or audit persistence fails.

workstreams.title: Question bank and assessment management UI synchronization
steps: Extend management contracts and forms for durable key display, canonical lesson/curriculum selection, relational skill mapping, provenance, duplicate conflict details, pinned assessment composition, and RowVersion.
Replace free-text or inferred mappings with IDs loaded from live curriculum, lesson, and skill APIs. Do not default missing selections to Math 12, a synthetic chapter, or a placeholder skill.
Build assessments by selecting approved question-bank records rather than creating assessment-private duplicate ContentQuestion rows. Preserve ordering and show the pinned version/fingerprint status.
Require explicit review before publish when duplicate, provenance, mapping, or changed-version warnings exist. Do not expose answer keys in learner-facing components or shared learner DTO types.
Handle loading, empty, validation, permission, duplicate conflict, stale-version conflict, API failure, and confirmed success explicitly; retain unsaved input on recoverable 409 responses.
Remove synthetic explanation text and false-success toasts. Show success only after the API confirms the persisted representation and refresh returns the same mapping.
Keep management flows keyboard accessible and usable at 390px while reusing existing tokens and components.

workstreams.title: Learner frontend API authority and no synthetic fallback
steps: For authenticated learners, make the API the authority for attempt identity, selected questions, resume state, answer persistence, finalization, grading, and results. Local storage may be a transparent cache only and must not create official attempts or scores.
Remove client-side grading and client-supplied IsCorrect/score fields from network contracts. Clear or ignore cached answer-key fields and reconcile cache state from server RowVersion after refresh.
Render active questions only from learner-safe DTOs and reveal correctness, correct answers, and explanations only from an authorized finalized-result response.

When no eligible questions or published assessment exists, show a genuine empty state and disable start. On API failure, show error/retry without generating fallback questions, assessments, IDs, scores, or completion events.
Handle 401/403 ownership failures and 409 stale/finalized conflicts without overwriting server state or displaying success.
Verify refresh/resume persistence, duplicate-submit idempotency, accessibility, and mobile 390px behavior across practice and quiz routes.

workstreams.title: P05 security, migration, and regression verification
steps: Add unit tests for normalization and fingerprint stability, Unicode/whitespace/option canonicalization, source keys, duplicate races, mapping consistency, assessment composition, state transitions, server grading, idempotency, and RowVersion conflicts.

Add isolated SQL integration tests for migration preservation, existing duplicate retention, VNHSGE provenance, FK validation, transactional audit, published-version pinning, immutable finalized attempts, concurrent finalize, and retry behavior.

Add API tests proving no pre-submission payload or direct endpoint leaks CorrectAnswer, explanation-derived answers, grading rules, or snapshot keys; cover 401, cross-user 403/404, staff RBAC, self-review denial, 409, and persistence failure.

Add frontend tests for live mapping selectors, duplicate and concurrency recovery, authenticated API authority, no-question empty state, API failure, refresh persistence, and absence of answer-bearing fields before finalization.

Add Playwright scenarios for question create/map/review/publish, assessment composition, learner start/resume/finalize/review, duplicate prevention, 401/403, two-user isolation, stale conflict, API failure, refresh persistence, and 390px mobile.

Run P02, P03, and P04 regression suites plus frontend frozen install/lint/test/build and backend restore/build/unit/integration gates. Use only per-run StudyAIDb_Clean_{GUID}; summarize logs into TEST-SUMMARY.json and report unavailable gates as NOT RUN.

Run read-only Codex review with the prescribed attempt limit, remediate blocking findings, update PHASE-P05 and PROGRESS with exact evidence, and require human approval before migration, merge, or phase advancement.

acceptance_criteria: Every existing question, assessment association, attempt, response, score, content revision, source batch, and VNHSGE provenance record remains present and addressable after P05 migration.
Existing duplicates are reported and preserved; no automated migration merges, deletes, re-IDs, or silently repoints historical records.
Every new or edited active question receives a server-generated immutable durable key, versioned fingerprint, and RowVersion, with transactional duplicate prevention under concurrent writes.

Question-to-skill mapping uses QuestionSkill foreign keys; lesson, chapter, subject, grade, skill, and curriculum mappings are validated against real IDs with no MetadataJson substring authority or hardcoded subject fallback.
Assessment composition uses ordered reusable question mappings pinned to a question version/fingerprint, while legacy AssessmentId relationships remain compatible during migration.
Pre-finalization learner APIs and UI contain no correct answer, answer-bearing explanation, grading rule, or protected snapshot data.

Authenticated learner attempts are created and graded server-side; clients cannot choose another user, submit scores or IsCorrect, change assessment identity, or finalize an assessment with arbitrary questions.

Finalization is atomic and idempotent, and every finalized attempt, response, identity field, score, and completion timestamp is immutable; stale or repeated mutations return HTTP 409 without data loss.
Learner A cannot read, resume, submit, finalize, or review learner B's attempts or responses; staff operations enforce existing RBAC and independent-review rules.

Published questions and assessments require complete provenance, verified mappings, and approved workflow state; VNHSGE source/license fields are retained unchanged unless an explicitly audited correction is approved.
Question-bank and assessment UIs use live curriculum/lesson/skill IDs, handle duplicate and RowVersion conflicts, and never show false success after API or persistence failure.
No runtime path creates synthetic questions, assessments, mappings, IDs, scores, explanations, or mastery evidence when data is empty or an API fails.

P05 unit, integration, frontend, and Playwright coverage includes happy path, validation, duplicate race, 401, 403, 404, 409, API failure, refresh persistence, two-user isolation, answer-leak checks, immutable finalization, and mobile 390px.
P02, P03, and P04 regression gates pass, or failures/unavailable gates are logged and remain blocking.
Migration application to StudyAIDb, merge, and phase advancement occur only after reviewed SQL, backup/rollback preparation, test evidence, Codex review, and explicit human approval.
database_safety_notes: ENV-01/ENV-02 are blocking. Planning and review are read-only. StudyAIDb must not be touched by automated tests, fixtures, Playwright, imports, seeds, bootstrap, migration rehearsal, reset, truncate, drop, or automatic migration. The static StudyAIDb_E2E and StudyAIDb_Dev names are also forbidden. Every integration, migration, and browser run must fail closed unless the resolved target is a uniquely owned StudyAIDb_Clean_{GUID}, provisioned atomically with an ownership manifest and cleaned up only by its owning run using bounded LOCK_TIMEOUT behavior—never SINGLE_USER WITH ROLLBACK IMMEDIATE. Rehearsal data must include representative historical questions, duplicates, VNHSGE provenance, attempts, responses, and scores, with before/after count and checksum evidence. Applying P05 to StudyAIDb requires a separately approved controlled-maintenance window, verified backup, reviewed forward and rollback SQL, dry-run evidence, and post-migration integrity checks.
